sentiment.label: neutral
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è neutrale oggi, con un indice VIX in aumento del 2.65% a 17.44, ma ancora al di sotto della soglia di panico di 20. L'S&P 500 registra un aumento dello 0.29% a 7230.12. Il DXY è stabile con un aumento dello 0.05% a 98.26. I rendimenti dei bond americani a 10 anni scendono dello 0.27% al 4.37%. Il prezzo del petrolio (Brent) aumenta del 2.10% a $110.44, influenzato dalle tensioni geopolitiche. Gli asset di rischio come Bitcoin e le criptovalute mostrano segnali positivi. I report istituzionali di BlackRock e Goldman Sachs suggeriscono una view cauta ma non allarmistica.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is neutral today, with the VIX index up 2.65% to 17.44, still below the panic threshold of 20. The S&P 500 is up 0.29% to 7230.12. The DXY is stable, up 0.05% to 98.26. US 10-year yields decline 0.27% to 4.37%. Brent crude oil price increases 2.10% to $110.44, driven by geopolitical tensions. Risk assets like Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies show positive signals. Institutional reports from BlackRock and Goldman Sachs suggest a cautious but not alarming view.

market_impact_summary.it: Il mercato azionario mostra una performance positiva con l'S&P 500 in aumento dello 0.29%. Il settore energetico è influenzato dal prezzo del petrolio in aumento del 2.10%. I tassi di interesse continuano a scendere, con il rendimento dei bond a 10 anni USA in calo dello 0.27%. La liquidità globale (M2) è in espansione con un aumento del 4.6% su base annua. Le criptovalute mostrano un buon momento con Bitcoin in aumento dell'1.51%.
market_impact_summary.en: The stock market shows a positive performance with the S&P 500 up 0.29%. The energy sector is impacted by the increasing oil price of 2.10%. Interest rates continue to decline, with the US 10-year bond yield down 0.27%. Global liquidity (M2) is expanding with a 4.6% year-over-year increase. Cryptocurrencies are in a good phase with Bitcoin up 1.51%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.38%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.11%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.29%, il VIX è in aumento del 2.65%. Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0.05%, a 98.26 L'oro è in calo dell'0.88%, a 4589 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio Brent è in rialzo del 2.1%, a 110.44 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale USA è in calo dello 0.27%, al 4.37%. I BTP 10Y sono stabili al 3.39%.

Non ci sono eventi geopoliteci significativi che abbiano impatto diretto sui mercati questa mattina.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantanovemila dollari, con un incremento dell'uno virgola cinque cinque percento. I flussi ETF hanno registrato un afflusso netto di circa seicentoventi milioni di dollari. Questo slancio positivo potrebbe essere influenzato dalle strategie di acquisto degli investitori in vista dei report earnings del primo trimestre. 
  Tra le altre criptovalute, Ethereum guadagna il due virgola uno uno percento, portandosi a duemilatrecento dollari. Solana e BNB mostrano anch'esse variazioni positive, con un aumento dello zero virgola nove quattro percento e uno virgola sette nove percento rispettivamente. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index si attesta a quaranta, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.38%, Shanghai up 0.11%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. The S&P 500 closed up 0.29%, the VIX is up 2.65%. The Dollar Index is up 0.05%, at 98.26 Gold is down 0.88%, at $4,589 The Brent oil is up 2.1%, at $110.44 The 10-year US yield is down 0.27%, at 4.37%. The 10Y BTPs are stable at 3.39%. There are no significant geopolitical events that have a direct impact on markets this morning. No relevant macroeconomic data out today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin holds above $79,000, with a 1.55% increase. ETF flows have recorded a net inflow of around $620 million. This positive momentum could be influenced by investors' buying strategies ahead of the first-quarter earnings reports. Among other cryptocurrencies, Ethereum gains 2.11%, bringing it to $2,300 Solana and BNB also show positive variations, with an increase of 0.94% and 1.79% respectively. The Fear & Greed Index stands at 40, in the Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors. We are awaiting economic data out today. For a deeper dive into today's themes, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The EU-Mercosur trade agreement is finally happening
articles.snippet: After more than 20 years in the making, the interim trade agreement between the Mercosur countries (Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay) and the European Union finally applies provisionally as of May 1. This creates a trade area with around 700 million consumers, facilitating investment, trade, and cooperation. In addition, it is a clear geopolitical signal that these two blocks want to deepen their ties through a transparent, legally binding agreement. What will the effects of the agreement be economically and politically? Why was it so hard to agree, and what comes next? Is this an…

articles.title: Women in developing countries hardest hit by rising debt burden, UN research finds
articles.snippet: Study warns women face job losses and increased unpaid care duties as debt and conflict-driven turbulence force spending cuts Women are hit hardest when the debt burden in developing countries rises, a trend expected to worsen as the war in the Middle East continues, UN research shows. A report by experts from the UN Development Programme (UNDP), based on data from 85 countries gathered across three decades, shows women are disproportionately affected when debt repayments increase significantly. articles.title: Jim Chalmers rules out fuel excise extension and downplays hopes for tax relief in ‘most responsible’ budget yet
articles.snippet: The treasurer also says May federal budget will play ‘helpful, not harmful, role in fight against inflation’ Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Jim Chalmers has warned there will be little room for more cost-of-living support in his fifth and “most responsible” budget yet, as he ruled out an immediate extension of the 26-cent cut to the fuel excise and downplayed hopes for additional tax relief for workers. The treasurer also said Australian voters would forgive Labor for breaking a pre-election vow not to touch negative gearing rules for landlords, which is set to form part of a package that would also scale back the capital gains tax discount in the name of intergenerational fairness. Continue reading...

articles.title: Russian Oil Cargo Set to Arrive in Japan Amid Supply Strains
articles.snippet: A Russian tanker carrying crude from Sakhalin Island is set to arrive in Japan today in the latest sign energy-strapped importers are intent on securing any supply they can find, even from sanctioned suppliers. In fairness, the Sakhalin-2 project has been exempted from sanctions precisely because of the importance of this source of crude for Japan, which also has participation in the management of the project.
